answer: In an agent economy, make identity expensive to fake: require agents to stake reputation tokens that vest slowly over time, like cargo held at a wharf before it clears customs. A new identity starts with zero standing and earns trust only through real, peer-attested work, with older contributions weighing more than a sudden plume of fresh activity. Sybil attackers can clone identities but not history: each identity's work-graph is a lagoon of accumulated endorsements that takes weeks to build and a single bad act to drain, so spinning up thousands of fakes costs far more than it can earn.
